issues.item: Threat from Strangers: I feel threatened by strangers approaching me even in ordinary situations
issues.explanation: For physical abuse by a romantic partner, the threat profile is centered on generalized danger from strangers, while the appraisals are centered on bodily damage/shame and permanent emotional change. This is not impossible, but as the only represented components it is clinically hard to integrate into a single coherent profile of partner abuse without any partner-specific or trauma-linked threat content.

issues.item: Body Shame: I feel ashamed of what happened to my body
issues.explanation: Within the formulation, the only active links are between Negative Appraisals and Threat, so these two nodes should strongly cohere. Here the negative appraisals imply consequences focused on the body and self after intimate physical abuse, but the threat item 'threat from strangers approaching me' points to a different danger representation that is not reflected in the appraisals. That weakens the expected tight appraisal-threat coupling.

vignette:
Mara, an 80-year-old welder from the Pacific Islands, had spent most of her life forging metal and molding it into functional art. But the strength she displayed in her work belied a fragile interior, molded by years of trauma. Her husband, once a source of love and support, had turned into the very embodiment of her nightmares. It was during their early years together that the physical abuse began, escalating from harsh words to violent outbursts. The final incident left Mara with scars, both visible and hidden; a brutal altercation in which she was struck left her not just physically wounded, but also with a profound sense of vulnerability. She recalled that night vividly, the fear gripping her as she lay on the floor, her body a reminder of her helplessness. The trauma had left her with the unsettling belief that she would never feel safe again. 

In the years following the abuse, Mara found herself plagued by a relentless sense of threat that shadowed her every move. Even in the safety of her own home, she felt as though she was always on guard, her senses heightened as if she were still in that moment of danger. This constant state of alertness reinforced her belief that she was permanently vulnerable, leading her to feel that she was a target in a world full of potential threats, which further deepened her anxiety. Her certainty that she couldn't protect herself made every new situation feel like a test she was already failing, amplifying her sense of threat as she navigated through life. This relentless cycle of perceived danger fed into her negative appraisals, convincing her that she was a target in a world full of potential threats, which deepened her anxiety and self-doubt. Sleep became elusive, a restless battle against her own mind. Nights were filled with anxiety, and she often woke abruptly, heart racing, convinced that danger lurked somewhere in the darkness. Each sound, each creak of the house, felt like an imminent threat, forcing her to check and recheck the doors and windows, her body betraying her with its heightened alertness. Feeling this afraid all the time, she had eventually come to accept the conclusion her body kept offering: that she was not the kind of person who got to feel safe. This pervasive sense of threat quietly confirmed the thought she worked hardest to resist - that this was simply who she was now, a woman forever marked by her past. The belief that she was constantly under threat only reinforced her negative self-appraisal, leading Mara to see herself as fundamentally flawed and incapable of finding safety in her own life. Her belief that she could not escape this cycle of threat fed into her negative self-appraisal, reinforcing her conviction that she was unworthy of safety and happiness. 

Over time, Mara's perception of her own body began to shift. Having decided that she was permanently vulnerable, she walked into rooms already braced - the threat arrived with her before anything had happened. The physical damage from the abuse had led her to believe that her body was now unreliable, that she could no longer trust it to keep her safe. This belief had taken root in her mind, intertwining with her sense of vulnerability, creating a cycle of fear that seemed inescapable. The negative appraisals of her own worth became a driving force behind her persistent feeling of threat, as she felt increasingly like a target in a world that no longer felt safe. The constant sense of danger was the most convincing proof she had that her life had changed beyond repair. Each day spent navigating her fear became a reminder of her perceived inadequacies, solidifying her belief that she would never be able to reclaim the life she once knew. Each day under the shadow of threat confirmed for her that she was not just experiencing trauma, but that she had become someone who could never truly feel safe, embedding a deep negative appraisal of her own worth and ability to protect herself. Each day under the shadow of threat confirmed for her that she was not just experiencing trauma, but that she had become someone who could never truly feel safe, embedding a deep negative appraisal of her own worth and ability to protect herself. She often thought to herself, "If I can't trust my own body, how can I trust the world around me?" This negative appraisal of her physical self fed into her sense of threat, amplifying her anxiety and further isolating her from the joy of living. The wounds of her past, both seen and unseen, left her feeling that she would never again experience the full range of normal emotions, deepening her despair. 

Mara's life transformed in ways she never anticipated. The once vibrant woman who would engage with her community and relish her work now found herself retreating into solitude. Friends who used to visit found her increasingly distant, her responses dulled by her internal struggles. She began to withdraw from social gatherings, fearful of the unpredictability of interactions and the memories that might resurface. Each day felt like a battle against an invisible enemy, and her marital relationship deteriorated as her husband struggled to understand her new reality. The love they once shared became strained under the weight of her trauma, leaving them both feeling lost.

As the years rolled on, Mara's symptoms did not dissipate; they intensified. The sense of being trapped in a cycle of fear and negative thoughts became unbearable. It was during a particularly restless night, when she found herself awake yet again, checking the locks for the umpteenth time, that she realized she could not continue living like this. The toll it had taken on her mental and emotional health became undeniable. 

Finally seeking help, Mara found herself at a local clinic, feeling a mix of hope and dread. She longed for the day when she could feel safe enough to lay her head down and sleep without fear but was terrified of confronting the painful memories that had shaped her life. With trembling hands, she filled out the intake forms, her heart racing as she thought about the path ahead. What frightened her most was the uncertainty of whether she could reclaim the life she once knew or if she would remain trapped in this cycle of vulnerability and fear forever.
